title: EA-CORPORA-21 — The Twenty-First Seating: The Maya Codices, the Popol Vuh, the Colonial Maya Books and the Florentine Codex; the Egyptian Book of the Dead and Earlier Egyptian, Each in Its Original Language
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Seven seats on the originals shelf, each in the language of its witness: the Maya codices (Dresden in the Saxon State Library's own photographs, through the World Digital Library; Paris in Rosny's facsimile of 1887–88; Madrid in Rosny's photographs of 1883 and Brasseur's chromolithographs of 1869); the Popol Vuh in Francisco Ximénez's K'iche' manuscript (Newberry Library, Ayer MS 1515) and Brasseur's first edition of the K'iche' text (1861); the Chilam Balam of Chumayel in Gordon's facsimile (1913), the Annals of the Cakchiquels in Brinton's edition (1885) and the Rabinal Achí in Brasseur's (1862); the Florentine Codex, Sahagún's General History of the Things of New Spain in Nahuatl and Spanish, all twelve books; the Egyptian Book of the Dead in Lepsius's Turin papyrus (1842), the Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum's facsimile (1894) and Budge's reproduction (1913), Budge's hieroglyphic Theban recension (1898) and Naville's introduction (1886); and Earlier Egyptian in its script, the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae's 12,773 sentences in Unicode hieroglyphs (CC BY-SA 4.0), with Sethe's Pyramid Texts III–IV. The second of three seatings from one request. What could not be reached is named: Naville's and Sethe's text volumes, the Grolier Codex, and the Deir ʿAlla Balaam text, whose one open witness Wikimedia refused to serve.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Sources located, fetched, checked against the Internet Archive's published md5 sums and against their front matter, assembled into seats, hashed and indexed, and every locus found in the seated text, all in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction. The selection — Mayan texts, the Book of the Dead, the fragments of Balaam, and yes to the rest offered, originals in the original language or as close to it as possible — is Lee Sharks's. CC-BY-4.0 applies to this record and the seat records; each payload carries its own licence, stated per seat (the TLA corpus CC BY-SA 4.0, redistributed under it).
methodology: Sources located on the Internet Archive (advanced search; item metadata read for access restriction, volume and files), in the Library of Congress's World Digital Library collection (its JSON item records), at FAMSI and on Hugging Face. Each item's front matter read against the edition claimed; an item that holds another volume than the one sought is seated as what it is. Every Internet Archive file checked against the Archive's md5; every Library of Congress and FAMSI file against the length its server states; the TLA file against the sha256 Hugging Face publishes. OCR layers seated as fetched, uncorrected, the scans the witnesses; image files without a text layer seated as images; the TLA reading text derived from its JSONL by code. Every file hashed into its seat's MANIFEST.sha256; every verified locus is a string found in the seated text by rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-21/seat.py.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a seated file differs from the file at the origin its source.json names (for Internet Archive files, if its md5 differs from the Archive's); if an edition statement misstates the front matter of the file it describes; if a verified locus cannot be found in the seated text; if an item stated public domain in the United States was published in or after 1931; if a Library of Congress or FAMSI file differs in length from the file at its origin; if the TLA file's sha256 differs from the one its repository publishes; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-21 seats six collections on the archive's originals shelf, from Mesoamerica and Egypt, each in the language of its witness: 28 works. The three Maya hieroglyphic codices are seated whole: the Dresden Codex in the Saxon State Library's own photographs, through the World Digital Library; the Paris Codex in Léon de Rosny's facsimile (1887–88); and the Madrid Codex in Rosny's photographs (1883) with Brasseur de Bourbourg's chromolithographs (1869). The Popol Vuh, the K'iche' book of the council, is seated in its one surviving witness, Francisco Ximénez's manuscript of about 1701–03 (Newberry Library, Ayer MS 1515), with the K'iche' and the Spanish in facing columns, and in Brasseur's first edition of the K'iche' text (1861). Three Maya books of the colonial period are seated in their own languages: the Yucatec Chilam Balam of Chumayel in G. B. Gordon's facsimile (1913), the Kaqchikel Annals of the Cakchiquels in Daniel Brinton's edition (1885), and the K'iche' Rabinal Achí in Brasseur's (1862). The Florentine Codex, Bernardino de Sahagún's General History of the Things of New Spain in Nahuatl and Spanish, is seated in all twelve books from the World Digital Library. The Egyptian Book of the Dead is seated in Richard Lepsius's Turin papyrus (1842), the edition that numbered its chapters, in the Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum's facsimile (1894) and Budge's reproduction (1913), in Budge's hieroglyphic text of the Theban recension (1898) and in Édouard Naville's introduction (1886). Earlier Egyptian is seated in its script: the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae's 12,773 sentences in Unicode hieroglyphs with transliteration (CC BY-SA 4.0), with Kurt Sethe's Pyramid Texts, volumes III and IV. Naville's and Sethe's text volumes, the Grolier Codex and the Deir ʿAlla text of Balaam son of Beor are named as not seated, with the reasons. It is the second of three seatings from one request, after EA-CORPORA-20.
